newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Cellular bid shows promise of Brazil telcoms.
newsitem.headline: Cellular bid shows promise of Brazil telcoms.

text.p: The enormous price paid this week by a U.S.-led group for a cellular phone concession in Sao Paulo shows the promise of Brazil's ambitious plan to sell-off its vast Telebras system, analysts said Thursday.

The BCP consortium, made up of BellSouth Corp and Brazilian firms Banco Safra, O Estado de Sao Paulo and Splice, paid 2.6 billion reais ($2.45 billion) Wednesday for the 20-year concession, nearly four times the government's asking price.
The concession will allow the group to operate on the B Band frequency in South America's leading cellular phone market.

The offer, which most analysts did not expect to exceed 2.2 billion reais, was a clear sign that investors will be willing to pay a lot more for Telebras and its subsidiaries, Telesp in particular, when the firms go to the auction block in the near future.

"The very high price paid for the license for the Sao Paulo metropolitan area gives us a good idea of the premium strategic investors would be willing to pay for Telesp, relative to other operators, once the company is put up for sale," analyst Luiz Carvalho at Morgan Stanley Dean Witter said in a report.
Telesp covers metropolitan Sao Paulo, Brazil's wealthiest area, and is expected to be the first Telebras operating company to be privatized.
The result of the Sao Paulo Band B bidding process prompted banks and brokerages to issue reports reiterating their buy recommendations on Telebras and Telesp stocks. at 1230 local time/1530 GMT.

Analysts were also delighted by the winning bid for the Sao Paulo area because the rates offered by the group, only slightly lower than those charged by Telesp -- which currently enjoys a monopoly in the city -- would not trigger a price war.
"As they (the rates) were set only slightly below Telesp's existing rates, Telesp is unlikely to face significant rate pressures when competition begins," Morgan Stanley's Carvalho said.

Analysts also think the price paid by the BellSouth-led group will serve as a benchmark for the valuation of the Band A cellular business, which will also be offered to private investors after the Band B sell-off is completed.

Although a model for the privatization of Telebras and its subsidiaries has not been designed yet, some experts believe that cellular and wireline services provided by the federal system would be sold off simultaneously.
So far the Communications Ministry has announced the winning groups for three of a total of 10 regional cellular concessions that it plans to tender out.

In addition to Sao Paulo, whose winner was announced Wednesday, the ministry said a consortium led by Italy's Stet won the contract to operate cellular services in an area covering the northeastern states of Bahia and Sergipe.
The first contract, covering central western Brazil, was granted in early June to the Americel group, which includes Bell Canada, a unit of BCE Inc.
So far, revenue from the sale of Band B cellular concessions has totalled $3.0 billion.
ING Barings expects proceeds from the sale of the remaining seven concession areas to total $4.0 billion.

"Added to CVRD sale proceeds of $3.1 billion, (the cellular concession sales) would alone exceed the government's ambitious plan of earning an all-time record of $10 billion with privatization proceeds this year," ING said.
